items.title: Koszul regularity is preserved by a flat base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that both versions of Koszul regularity of a sequence of elements, the version relative to a module and the absolute one, survive base change along a flat ring map: if f_1 to f_r is M-H_1-regular or M-Koszul-regular over R and S is a flat R-algebra, then the images of the f_i are N-H_1-regular or N-Koszul-regular for N = M tensor over R with S (statement lines 7336-7347). The proof is eight lines (proof lines 7350-7357) and it is a two-step identification: the Koszul complex of the sequence over S is the base change of the Koszul complex over R, and this identity together with associativity of the tensor product rewrites (K(f) tensor M) tensor S as K(phi(f)) tensor N, which is exactly the complex whose homology has to vanish. What a reader has to check is the second identity, since the first is the definition of the base changed sequence; the author displays the conclusion of both steps and stops there.
